claim: Direct class-equation plan solved: Let \(p\) be a prime and let \(G\) be a finite group of order \(p^n\) for some integer \(n\ge 1\). Then the order of \(Z(G)\) is divisible by \(p\), and \(Z(G)\) contains a nonidentity element.
evidence:
Let (G) act on its underlying set by conjugation: for (g,xin G), set (gcdot x=gxg^{-1}). The orbits of this action are the conjugacy classes. The orbit of (x) has one element exactly when (gxg^{-1}=x) for every (gin G), which is equivalent to (xin Z(G)).

For (xin G), define its centralizer by
[
C_G(x)={gin G:gx=xg}.
]
This is a subgroup of (G). The map from the set of left cosets (G/C_G(x)) to the conjugacy class of (x), given by
[
gC_G(x)longmapsto gxg^{-1},
]
is well-defined and bijective. Indeed, replacing (g) by (gc) with (cin C_G(x)) does not change (gxg^{-1}); and if (gxg^{-1}=hxh^{-1}), then (h^{-1}gin C_G(x)), so (gC_G(x)=hC_G(x)). Thus the conjugacy class of (x) has cardinality
[
[G:C_G(x)]= rac{|G|}{|C_G(x)|}.
]

The left cosets of any subgroup of a finite group partition the group and all have the same cardinality as the subgroup. Consequently (|C_G(x)|) divides (|G|=p^n), so (|C_G(x)|=p^m) for some integer (m) with (0le mle n). If (x
otin Z(G)), then (C_G(x)
e G), hence (m<n). Therefore every non-singleton conjugacy class has cardinality
[
[G:C_G(x)]=p^{,n-m},
]
which is divisible by (p).

Choose one representative (x_i) from each non-singleton conjugacy class, where the finite list may be empty. Since the conjugacy classes partition (G), and the singleton conjugacy classes are precisely the elements of (Z(G)), the class equation is
[
|G|=|Z(G)|+sum_i [G:C_G(x_i)].
]
Every term in the sum is divisible by (p), and (|G|=p^n) is divisible by (p) because (nge1). Hence (|Z(G)|) is divisible by (p).

Finally, the identity element belongs to (Z(G)), so (|Z(G)|ge1). Since (|Z(G)|) is a positive multiple of the prime (p), and (pge2), we have (|Z(G)|ge2). Thus (Z(G)) contains an element distinct from the identity.
